extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent practitioners (patent owners and third-party requesters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examining and conducting ex parte reexamination proceedings of U.S. patents, including use of admissions, claim construction, 35 U.S.C. 112 compliance, new matter, claim broadening under 35 U.S.C. 305, and the use of previously cited art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent owner admissions in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions by the patent owner in the record as to matters affecting patentability may be utilized in a reexamination proceeding; see 37 CFR 1.104(c)(3). An admission as to what is in the prior art is simply that, an admission, and requires no independent proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissions may be used to determine the scope and content of the prior art in conjunction with patents and printed publications; they can be used to interpret or modify a prior art patent or printed publication. Admissions can reside in the patent file, be presented during reexamination, or arise in litigation. A third party may not submit admissions of the patent owner made outside the record (file or court record) because such submissions are outside scope of reexamination. Ignoring admissions would prevent proper determination of scope and content of prior art as required by Graham v. John Deere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim interpretation in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claims will be examined only on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications applied under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103. During reexamination, claims are given the broadest reasonable interpretation consistent with the specification and limitations in the specification are not read into the claims (In re Yamamoto).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reexamination involving claims of an expired patent, apply Phillips (ordinary and customary meaning to a person having ordinary skill in the art) since expired claims are not subject to amendment. The statutory presumption of validity (35 U.S.C. 282) has no application in reexamination (In re Etter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit scope of 35 U.S.C. 112 examination to amendatory matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Where new claims are presented or any part of the disclosure is amended, the claims of the reexamination proceeding are to be examined for compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112, but consideration of 112 issues should be limited to the amendatory (e.g., new language) matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim amended or new that contains a limitation not found in the original patent claim should be considered for 35 U.S.C. 112 compliance only with respect to that limitation. A term in an original claim cannot be examined as too broad in a new or amended claim unless the amendatory matter creates the issue. If a dependent claim is rewritten as an independent claim in reexamination, that independent claim cannot be examined as to 35 U.S.C. 112 unless the rewriting raises a new question (e.g., lack of antecedent). See MPEP §2163 - §2173.05(v) for extensive guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: New matter prohibition under 35 U.S.C. 132
rubrics_metrics.description: 35 U.S.C. 305 provides for examination under 35 U.S.C. 132, which prohibits the introduction of new matter into the disclosure. The question of new matter should be considered in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If new matter is added to claims or affects claim limitations, the claims should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, first paragraph, for failing the written description requirement. See MPEP §2163.06 regarding relationship between written description and new matter prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the specification must comply with 35 U.S.C. 112
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the specification is amended in a reexamination proceeding, the examiner should ensure that the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112 are met because an amendment can redefine claim terms so that claims become unclear or unsupported by the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amendment to the specification can result in failure of the claims to comply with 35 U.S.C. 112 even if the claims themselves are not amended. Also, an amendment to the specification must not enlarge the scope of the claims (see separate enlargement criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims in proceeding must not enlarge scope of the patent (35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: When new or amended claims are presented or any part of the disclosure is amended, the claims of the reexamination proceeding should be examined under 35 U.S.C. 305 to determine whether they enlarge the scope of the original claims. 'No proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim of the patent will be permitted in a reexamination proceeding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A presented claim enlarges the scope where it is broader than each and every claim of the patent. A claim is broader if it contains within its scope any conceivable product or process that would not have infringed the original patent. A claim is broadened if broader in any one respect even if narrower in others. Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 305 should be made (Form paragraph 22.11). Identify claim limitations considered to broaden scope and explain in bracket 2 per MPEP §2258.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and explain limitations that broaden claim scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim limitations considered to broaden the scope should be identified and explained in bracket 2 of the Office action (see MPEP §2258).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.11 and in bracket 2 insert the claim limitations considered broadening; provide explanation/mapping for why those limitations broaden compared to the patent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling patents subject to prior Office or court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some of the patent claims have been the subject of a prior Office or court decision, special handling is required; claims not subject to reexamination because of prior adjudication should be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2242. For 'live' claims dependent on claims not subject to reexamination, see MPEP §2260.01. If grounds are set forth in a prior Office or Federal Court decision which are not based on patents or printed publications, the examiner's Office action should clearly state those grounds have not been examined as they are not based on patents/printed publications (see 37 CFR 1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination generally limited to 'live' claims requested
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office’s determination in the order for reexamination and examination stage will generally be limited solely to review of the 'live' claims (existing claims not held invalid by a final decision) for which reexamination has been requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 302 requires the request to set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested. If requester fails to apply art to certain claims, requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of those claims. The Office may, at its sole discretion, reexamine claims not requested or initiate reexamination on its own (35 U.S.C. 303(a)). If prior art discovered during reexamination raises SNQ as to non-requested claims, such claims may be added at the Office's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction requirements not proper in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements cannot be made in a reexamination proceeding since no statutory basis exists for restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of claims to a 'separate and distinct' invention would be considered enlargement of the scope of the patent claims. See Ex parte Wikdahl and MPEP §1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary amendments permitted if incident to patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: There are matters ancillary to reexamination necessary and incident to patentability which will be considered; amendments may be made to the specification to correct certain failures when necessary to overcome a reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include correcting an inadvertent failure to claim foreign priority or the continuing status relative to a parent application if necessary to overcome a reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming foreign and domestic priority in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner may obtain right of foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) where a priority claim had been made before patent was granted by submitting a certified copy; similar provisions for domestic benefits under 35 U.S.C. 120 and 119(e) subject to filing petitions where required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For patents that matured from applications filed on or after Nov 29, 2000, to correct or claim certain priorities the owner must file a grantable petition for unintentionally delayed priority (37 CFR 1.55(c) or 1.78(a)(3)). A reexamination cannot be employed to add or correct a benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) when the application is no longer pending for patents matured from applications filed on or after Nov 29, 2000. No renewal of previously made priority/benefit claims is necessary during reexamination. See AIPA amendment to 35 U.S.C. 119(e)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship may be made during reexamination; if a petition under 37 CFR 1.324 is granted, the reexamination certificate will contain the appropriate change-of-inventorship information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.324 and MPEP §1481. The Certificate of Correction is effectively merged with the reexamination certificate; no separate Certificate of Correction will issue if reexamination certificate will contain the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131 and 1.132 may be utilized in a reexamination proceeding, with limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131 may not be used to 'swear back' of a reference patent if the reference patent is claiming the 'same invention' as the patent undergoing reexamination. In such situations, use affidavit under 37 CFR 1.130 or consider raising the issue via an interference or an appropriate reissue application (see MPEP §718 and §1449.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues not considered within scope of ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain issues (for example, questions of patentability based on public use or on sale, 'conduct issues', abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c), etc.) raised by the third party requester or the patent owner during reexamination may be noted but are not considered in the reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 22.03 to note that an issue is not within the scope of reexamination and will not be considered. The patentee may be advised to consider filing a reissue application if they wish the issue to be resolved. If such issues are independently discovered by the examiner but were not raised by the parties, they will not be noted in an Office action because 37 CFR 1.552(c) is only directed to issues 'raised by the patent owner or the third party requester.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexamination requests on patents after reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a request for reexamination is filed on a patent after it has been reissued, reexamination will be denied because the patent on which the request is based has been surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination of the reissued patent is desired, a new request based on the specification and claims of the reissue patent must be filed. Any amendment made by the patent owner to accompany the initial reexamination request or later prosecution should treat the changes made by the granted reissue patent as the text of the patent (all bracketing/underlining should be with respect to the reissue changes). See MPEP §2285 if reissue issues after filing of a request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check file history for previously cited/considered art ('old art') before rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: In the examining stage of reexamination, the examiner will consider whether claims are subject to rejection based on art; before making such a rejection the examiner should check the patent's file history to ascertain whether the art was previously cited/considered in an earlier concluded Office examination (referred to as 'old art').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'old art' coined in In re Hiniker. If the rejection will be based on combination of old art and new art, the rejection is proper (Hiniker). If old art provides the sole basis, different rules apply depending on whether reexamination was ordered on or after Nov 2, 2002 (see next criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexaminations ordered on or after Nov 2, 2002 — old art can alone raise SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered on or after Nov 2, 2002 (Pub. L. 107-273), reliance solely on old art as basis for a rejection does not necessarily preclude the existence of a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations whether an SNQ exists when based solely on old art shall be fact-specific. A SNQ may exist where the old art is presented/viewed in a new light or different way in view of material new argument/interpretation in the request. When an Office action first sets forth an SNQ based solely on old art, include form paragraph 22.01.01. In bracket 2 insert the old art being applied and in bracket 3 explain how and why that fact situation applies (e.g., old art presented in a new light). This form paragraph is used only the first time the already cited/considered art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reexaminations ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002 — Portola Packaging constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002, old art generally cannot be used as the sole basis for a rejection (subject to exceptions) per In re Portola Packaging; implement Portola-based procedures for ongoing reexaminations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior art was previously relied upon to reject a claim in a concluded prior related Office proceeding, the Office will not conduct reexamination based only on such prior art. If prior art was cited and its relevance to patentability actually discussed on the record in a prior related proceeding, reexamination based only on such prior art is precluded. Generalized 'state of the art' citations do not preclude reexamination. Procedures when determining termination for Portola: (a) ascertain order date, (b) determine what prior art was relied upon or cited & discussed in prior related proceedings, (c) base rejections at least in part on art not previously relied upon or discussed, (d) withdraw rejections based only on such previously relied-upon/discussed art, (e) terminate prosecution where only remaining rejections are based on such art. Director may search for new art before terminating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for unusual fact patterns involving old art
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases with unusual fact patterns (e.g., prior art cited but the examiner did not appreciate issues raised) should be brought to CRU or TC Director for determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusual fact patterns may include situations where a textbook was cited but only select information was discussed; if request relies on other information in the textbook that actually teaches the claims, it may be appropriate to rely on that other information to order/conduct reexamination. A request that merely provides a new interpretation of a previously relied-upon reference does not create an SNQ.
